items.t: Jensen Huang apologizes to Nvidia staff, saying he went ‘too far’ and is in therapy
items.d: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to the semiconductor giant in an all-hands meeting Tuesday morning, apologizing to staff for his conduct during his previous stint at the company’s helm and vowing to do better this time around.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Jensen Huang says he’s thankful for second chance at Nvidia employee meeting The CEO acknowledged that he had gone ‘too far’ with some of his workplace behavior and said he has been going to therapy every day, a source told NBC News. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Tech stocks take a dip as Jensen Huang comes back as Nvidia CEO 04:53 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 24, 2026, 11:11 PM EST By Jean Lee and Jared Perlo Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to the semiconductor giant in an all-hands meeting Tuesday morning, apologizing to staff for his conduct during his previous stint at the company’s helm and vowing to do better this time around. No company has impacted the world as deeply or profoundly as Nvidia, Huang said, according to an Nvidia employee who attended the meeting. Huang called the company’s story the most interesting in the world. According to the individual, Huang expressed contrition for his past behavior and was adamant that employees should follow the company’s code of conduct. The AI hardware leader resigned from the company Nov. 12 amid mounting scrutiny about alleged romantic relationships with subordinates and Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed. According to U.S. intelligence officials, Alice Huang is suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. He also said that he has been regularly attending therapy and that he had been deeply embarrassed about recent events, the source said. The CEO was met with an overwhelmingly positive reception, even receiving a standing ovation, according to the source. Huang’s return marked a nearly unprecedented case of corporate whiplash. After a wave of reports emerged stating that he had been involved in extramarital relationships — potentially with someone accused of being a Chinese intelligence asset — Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife in a letter sent to Nvidia employees and shared online Nov. 8. Jensen Huang outside the Hart Senate Office Building in Washington, D.C., in July. Finn Gomez / Getty “To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me,” Huang wrote at the time. “I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence.” Huang issued a personal statement Nov. 17, expressing remorse but professing his admiration for and dedication to Nvidia. Huang co-founded the semiconductor designer in 1993 and grew it into what was once the world’s most valuable company. items.t: Blanche calls Nvidia a ‘good corporate citizen’ while dodging questions on probe
items.d: Attorney General Todd Blanche praised Nvidia as a “good corporate citizen” while sidestepping questions about the Justice Department’s role in the president’s controversial decision to push for the reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang.
items.fullText: Trump administration Todd Blanche calls Nvidia a ‘good corporate citizen’ while dodging questions on investigation President Donald Trump had said the Justice Department had “exonerated” the chip giant’s newly reinstated CEO, Jensen Huang. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Blanche says he would have told Trump about any crimes Jensen Huang committed 01:22 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 24, 2026, 1:37 PM EST By Dareh Gregorian and Helen Graham Attorney General Todd Blanche on Tuesday praised Nvidia as a “good corporate citizen” while sidestepping questions about the Justice Department’s role in the president’s controversial decision to push for the reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang. President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he’d spoken to Blanche and “they did a pretty good investigation, and they felt that he himself was exonerated,” referring to Huang. Asked at an unrelated press conference about Trump’s remarks, Blanche said, “What the president said is that he talked to a lot of people going into the decision that he made to encourage the board to reinstate him,” before adding, “I’m not going to get into communications I have with the president about it.” He then said that what Trump was saying “is exactly right.” “To the extent that, that the department, that the Department of Justice had information that he was committing crimes or something like this, that is, that is, that’s just not, that’s something that I would have certainly told the president had it been true,” Blanche said. NBC News previously reported that Trump sought Blanche and Vice President JD Vance’s help in convincing Nvidia’s board to bring Huang back. An administration official said the attorney general told the president that the DOJ had no evidence of wrongdoing by Huang or the company. Trump and Vance gave Nvidia’s board information that informed its decision to reinstate Huang, a person familiar with the conversations said. The company’s announcement of the move cited input from “senior levels” of government that convinced the board members that Huang posted “no national security risk.” When asked if Huang — who’d resigned as CEO earlier this month after reports of extramarital affairs, including a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy — had been investigated, Blanche told reporters, “What does that mean?” “Had Huang been investigated for what?” he continued. “I don’t understand the question,” he said, adding, “It’s certainly not fair to him to just speculate about, about things or answer hypothetical questions. And so, so no.” Asked about whether an investigation into the the chip exporter, Singapore-based Megaspeed, that the alleged spy worked for was ongoing, Blanche continued in a similar vein. items.t: 코스피, 6% 폭락하며 ‘5천피’ 반납…‘젠슨 황 효과’ 하루 만에 끝나
items.fullText: 본문 경제 경제일반 코스피, 6% 폭락하며 ‘5천피’ 반납…‘젠슨 황 효과’ 하루 만에 끝나 김영배 기자 수정 2026-11-25 20:03 펼침 0:00 Your browser does not support the audio element. 코스피가 전날보다 308.52포인트(6.16%) 내린 4697.51에 마감한 25일 서울 중구 하나은행 본점 ‘하나 캔버스’에 이날 코스피가 표시되고 있다. 연합뉴스 광고 전날 급반등했던 코스피가 25일 6% 넘게 추락해 ‘5천피’를 반납했다. 젠슨 황의 엔비디아 최고경영자(CEO) 복귀에 따른 반짝 기대감은 하루 만에 끝났다. 이날 코스피는 전날보다 308.52(6.16%) 떨어진 4697.51을 기록했다. 지수는 전날 대비 197.03(3.94%) 떨어진 4809.00으로 출발해 하락 폭을 키웠다. 지수 급락에 오전 9시8분께 ‘매도 사이드카’(프로그램 매도호가 일시 효력정지)가 발동될 정도로 투자심리가 냉각됐다. 유가증권시장에서 외국인 투자자들은 1조9천억원에 가까운 순매도로 지수 하락을 주도했다. 기관(-7억)도 순매도에 가세했다. 개인 투자자들의 순매수(1조4천억원)는 지수를 뒷받침하기에 역부족이었다. 광고 전날 유가증권시장에서 6%대 상승하며 초강세를 보였던 삼성전자와 에스케이(SK)하이닉스는 이날 각각 9.87%, 11.05% 떨어지며 상승분을 고스란히 반납했다. 에스케이스퀘어(-11.19%), 엘지(LG)에너지솔루션(-1.91%), 삼성전기(-12.0%), 현대차(-2.00%), 케이비(KB)금융(-2.18%) 등 시가총액 상위 종목 대부분 약세를 기록했다. 바이오 대장주인 삼성바이오로직스(+5.66%)와 셀트리온(+3.83%)이 순환매 유입으로 상승 마감하며 그나마 바닥을 받쳤다. 이날 국내 증시 급락은 앞서 열린 미국 뉴욕 증시에서 나스닥 종합지수(-8%), 필라델피아 반도체 지수(-7.88%) 약세로 예견됐던 터였다. 인공지능(AI) 투자의 수익성에 대한 의구심, 젠슨 황에 대한 미국 상원의 청문회와 당국의 회계 조사 예고가 투자 심리를 짓눌렀다. 광고 광고 인공지능 부문 핵심 기업 중 하나인 앤트로픽의 주가는 상장 이후 처음으로 공모가(83달러) 아래로 떨어지며 투자심리 위축에 가세했다. 마이크론에 대한 투자의견 하향 조정과 2028년 메모리 공급과잉 의견 가능성이 글로벌 투자은행(IB) 쪽에서 제기된 것도 투자심리를 억누른 요인으로 꼽혔다. 델 테크놀로지스의 3분기 실적이 시장 예상치를 웃돌았고, 미국 증시에서 다우지수와 헬스케어·필수 소비재 등 경기 방어주가 상대적으로 강세를 보인 게 실낱 기대감을 남겼다. 이날 코스닥 지수는 전날보다 15.24(2.29%) 내린 650.64로 마감했다. 서울 외환시장에서 원-달러 환율은 전날보다 0.8원 오른 1343.2원에 주간 거래를 마쳤다. 외국인의 국내 주식 매도, 국제 유가 상승세가 환율을 밀어 올렸다. 광고 김영배 선임기자 kimyb@hani.co.kr
